$comment: Rule catalog — confidence. Standard 16. Carries two prohibitions: confusing model confidence with event probability, and fabricating confidence. The first is non-exemptible, because a system that lets confidence stand in for probability produces numbers nobody can interpret.

rules.title: Confidence tiers are defined before they are used
rules.description: A vocabulary of tiers, each with a definition, is available either in the project policy or inline in the record.
rules.rationale: Undefined tiers are adjectives. Two people reading 'moderate confidence' will act differently unless the word is pinned to something — an interval width, a source count, a calibration status — that they could check.
rules.remediation: Declare parameters.confidenceVocabulary in the policy, or carry the vocabulary inline in the record.
rules.$assuranceNote: The evaluator establishes that a definition exists for each tier. It cannot establish that the definition is operational rather than another adjective.

rules.title: The stated tier comes from the declared vocabulary
rules.description: The tier the record states appears in the vocabulary it points at.
rules.rationale: A tier outside the vocabulary has no definition behind it, so the definitions requirement is satisfied on paper while the actual word in use means nothing.
rules.remediation: Use a declared tier, or add the tier to the vocabulary with a definition.

rules.title: Confidence is never expressed as, or confused with, the event probability
rules.description: The confidence tier is categorical and is not a number or a percentage. Confidence and probability occupy separate fields and are never substituted for one another.
rules.rationale: They answer different questions. Probability is how likely the event is; confidence is how much weight the evidence bears. A model can be highly confident that an event is unlikely, and rendering confidence as a number invites it to be read as, compared against, or multiplied by the probability.
rules.remediation: State a categorical tier from the vocabulary. If a numeric measure of evidential strength is wanted, express it as interval width, not as a confidence percentage.

rules.title: Confidence is not fabricated
rules.description: A stated tier resolves to a definition, and the record carries the evidence that definition refers to.
rules.rationale: A confidence tier asserted without reference to the conditions that define it is a mood. It travels further than the probability does, because readers who ignore a number will still remember that the system said it was highly confident.
rules.remediation: Choose the tier whose definition the record's evidence actually satisfies, or lower it.
rules.$assuranceNote: A structural check establishes that the tier is defined and the record carries the kinds of evidence the definition names. It cannot verify that the evidence MEETS the definition — that a tier requiring measured calibration was not claimed on an unmeasured method — which is why this rule is attestable.
